newsitem.title: USA: Delta's Grinstein may not want CEO job - paper.
newsitem.headline: Delta's Grinstein may not want CEO job - paper.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc's next chief executive officer is not likely to be board member Gerald Grinstein, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said on Thursday.
The newspaper reported that Grinstein, former CEO of Western Airlines, has made it known inside Delta that he does not want an active management role in the No. 3 ranked U.S. airline.
Grinstein, 64, who lives in Seattle, is believed by some observers to have had a role in current CEO Ron Allen's decision to retire when his contract expires on July 31.

He heads a board committee charged with finding a replacement for Allen, whose unexpected departure was announced on Monday. In recent days, Grinstein himself has been seen by analysts and other observers as a possible candidate to replace Allen, at least on an interim basis.

While the reasons for Allen's departure remain a mystery, speculation has centered on reports of deteriorating relations between the CEO and outside board directors such as Grinstein. Some press reports have focused on an alleged attempt by Allen to replace Chief Financial Officer Thomas Roeck, a former Western Airlines executive, without notifying the board.
Delta officials were not immediately available to comment on the newspaper article.
